after: The working base is contained in Airtable, an online database program. Its linked tables organize Papers, Feedback Pathways, Models, and Review Papers. A paper record contains bibliographic information and curation notes: short summaries of its reported mechanism, experimental conditions, and relevance to feedback design. A feedback-pathway record describes a sensory influence on motor control, such as Ib feedback influencing the stance-to-swing transition, and links that description to supporting papers. A model record connects a computational implementation to its source literature; a review record summarizes literature relevant to the collection. Thus, a pathway identifies a mechanism, the linked papers supply its experimental support, and model records identify implementations to examine. These links organize evidence; they do not establish that every relationship has been entered or verified. Paper matching uses DOI where available and normalized titles otherwise. The paper-table view is shown in Appendix~\ref{app:sadb_records} (Figure~\ref{fig:sadb_explorer}).

before: I developed several software tools to aid in the development of a human-mimetic robot driven by a neural model of control. To do this, I built the following five systems. 1) I adapted the Gait2392 human model in OpenSIM to an equivalent model in the physics simulator MuJoCo. I then connected it to the SNS-Toolbox and tested it with a CPG controller. 2) I developed a simulated BPA-routed robot counterpart to the Gait2392 Model, also coupled to a CPG controller. 3) I combined the Li walker and Deng neural model with foot-contact feedback and tested it... 4) I built a graphical neural construction coupled to a maintained mechanical simulator; 5) I coupled the SolidWorks robot assembly to MATLAB BPA models and a neural controller. These tools enable controlled comparisons of neural organization across biological and artificial actuation. I developed the specific converted models, actuator interfaces, graphical-library elements, and circuit implementations below to build and test those connections. The capability table identifies the connections demonstrated and those still incomplete.
after:
I developed tools for connecting neural controllers to the mechanical models used in this project. The work addressed five integration tasks:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Convert the Gait2392 human model from OpenSim to MuJoCo and connect it to an SNS-Toolbox CPG controller.
    \item Couple a BPA-routed robot counterpart to a CPG controller so that artificial-actuator mechanics can be examined.
    \item Combine the Li walker mechanics, Deng neural organization, and foot-contact feedback, and test the resulting controller and mechanical interfaces.
    \item Construct neural circuits graphically in Simulink and connect them to mechanical simulations.
    \item Bring SolidWorks-derived mechanisms and MATLAB BPA models into the same development workflow as the neural controller.
\end{enumerate}
These tasks have different completion levels. The converted models, actuator-force calculation, graphical neural blocks, and selected interface tests are described below. Importing a mechanism or reproducing a rhythm does not establish that a complete coupled model walks. Table~\ref{tab:sns_capability} distinguishes the demonstrated interfaces from the combinations that still require integration and testing.
reason: Keep the advisor five-part structure but distinguish tasks from completed systems, remove tested-it ellipsis, and define graphical construction.
